title: Vedas, Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita
welcome_lead: From the Rig Veda's hymns to Krishna's counsel on the battlefield, encounter Hinduism's sacred texts.

final_note: You have heard ancient hymns and modern devotion. Hindu scripture is vast and layered.

walkthroughs.body_html: The four Vedas — Rig, Sama, Yajur and Atharva — span hymns, melodies, sacrificial formulas and household rituals. Composed in archaic Sanskrit, they are 'shruti' (heard) and were transmitted orally with extraordinary precision long before being written.

The principal Upanishads (e.g. Brihadaranyaka, Chandogya, Katha) developed philosophical reflection on Brahman, atman, karma and moksha from around 800-200 BCE. They inspired the Vedanta schools and continue to influence Hindu thought worldwide.

The Bhagavad Gita, set on the eve of the Kurukshetra battle, presents Krishna's teaching to Arjuna on dharma, action and devotion. It integrates karma, bhakti and jnana paths and remains the most widely read Hindu scripture, central to figures from Gandhi to modern teachers.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.
Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.

mcqs.q: What was the Augustine vs Pelagius dispute about original sin?
options: The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Original sin means Christians believe babies are evil.

Augustine argued humans inherit a corrupted nature from Adam (original sin) and cannot achieve salvation without grace; Pelagius argued humans retain free will to choose good without divine intervention and that sin is imitated, not inherited.
Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.
